why: k complete rows need k(k+1)/2 coins, which grows with k, so the answer is the largest k whose cost fits in n: a monotone yes/no question you can binary search over k, once per array element.
hints: Write down how many coins k full rows use. Is that quantity increasing in k?
Because k(k+1)/2 is increasing, 'can I build k rows?' is true up to some k and false after it. Binary search for the last true k.
Search k in [0, 2*10^5] (enough for n up to 10^9) for each element: O(m log n) total. A closed form floor((sqrt(8n+1)-1)/2) also works if you use math.isqrt to avoid float error.
pitfalls: Using float sqrt can be off by one for large n; use integer math.isqrt or binary search.
Return one answer per input element, in the same order.
